correctness.rationale: Actual RESULT.md gives a full Markov-chain proof. Within each part all neighborhoods agree; any tied part independently has positive probability of becoming monochromatic in one step, so every coloring reaches a corner with positive probability. For a>b>=c, smaller parts adopt the unique largest color, leading to consensus or a closed polarized two-cycle. For a=b>c the large parts strictly copy each other while the size-c part is independently uniformly redrawn, yielding one irreducible class of 2^(c+1) labeled states, period 2, uniform stationary law and fixed cut a(a+c). For a=b=c every nonconsensus corner has a positive-probability direct route to consensus. Finite-state reachability excludes further closed classes; no uniform hitting-time bound is needed. Independent full labeled 32-state transition-SCC computation for K_(2,2,1) produced sink sizes [1,1,4]; it does not replace all-size proof.
